themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints skyrocketed to 6 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 4700% spike (z-score: 17.76)—suggesting a coordinated poster campaign or enforcement gap in Central Harlem this week.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 17.76)
Statistically significant spike (z-score 17.76 indicates extreme anomaly)
First major spike of this type in recent baseline period
reporting_angles: On-the-ground canvass: where are the illegal posts concentrated? (commercial ads, political, other?)
Interview NYC Sanitation on enforcement resources and response time to illegal posting complaints this week

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Central Harlem
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 7 this week from a baseline of 0.8 per week—an 833% increase (z-score: 7.54)—marking an acute spike that warrants investigation into whether this reflects tag crews, property neglect, or enforcement withdrawal.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints this week vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.54)
Sharp one-week spike suggests concentrated activity or new crews
Aligns with broader street disorder signals (illegal posting, encampments)
reporting_angles: Identify hotspots: which streets or blocks are being targeted? Interview residents and business owners.
Interview NYPD and NYC Parks on graffiti removal responsiveness and whether crews have been spotted

themes_detail.label: Encampment Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints rose to 15 this week from a baseline of 4.8 per week—a 216% increase (z-score: 4.21)—indicating a potential uptick in street homelessness or density that aligns with CB budget requests for homeless services upgrades.
evidence: 15 encampment complaints this week vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.21)
Community Board has submitted recurring budget request to upgrade facilities for the homeless—unmet need signal
Timing aligns with seasonal warming; Gothamist reported rat sightings likely to rise as temps warm, suggesting outdoor encampments may be visible/reported more
reporting_angles: Map the encampment complaints: which parks, subway stations, or street blocks? Interview affected residents and outreach workers.
Interview Department of Homeless Services on shelter capacity in Central Harlem and why street encampments may be rising this week

themes_detail.label: Street-Level Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 5 last week from a baseline of 0.5 per week—a 900% increase (z-score: 5.2)—suggesting either increased enforcement activity, new vendor density, or resident complaints about street vending in Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.2)
Part of broader street disorder cluster (illegal posting, graffiti, encampments) pointing to environmental quality concerns
Could indicate new street vending activity or city enforcement campaign
reporting_angles: On-the-ground reporting: where are vendor enforcement complaints clustered? (125th Street corridor, subway stations?)
Interview NYC Department of Consumer Affairs on enforcement activity last week and whether there was a coordinated sweep

themes_detail.label: Missed Trash Collection Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints rose to 11 last week from a baseline of 2.2 per week—a 389% increase (z-score: 2.97)—indicating potential gaps in sanitation service coverage that compound street disorder issues this week.
evidence: 11 missed collection complaints last week vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 2.97)
Converges with graffiti, illegal posting, and encampment spikes to suggest broader environmental neglect
CB budget requests for new equipment for Parks & Rec and DEP capital projects suggest infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Verify: were specific sanitation routes missed last week? Interview NYC Sanitation on staffing or service changes.
Report from the street: visual confirmation of uncollected trash in affected blocks; interview residents on collection frequency
